key_insight: A single elastic fiber in microfluidic flow can become a bistable, memory-bearing "fluidic hysteron" through elastohydrodynamic feedback between deformation and hydraulic resistance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a passive way to build flow-based memory and switching elements for microfluidic logic, adaptive fluidic circuits, and distributed sensing without relying on solid-state buckling or external control.
method: Anchor one elastic fiber inside a microfluidic channel and drive it with viscous flow.
Use a parallel bypass channel as a geometric load line to tune bistability and hydraulic coupling.
Study arrays of fibers by varying channel geometry to observe collective switching behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a cusp-catastrophe onset of bistability for a single fiber and a geometry-driven transition in arrays from noninteracting Preisach-like behavior with return point memory to interacting avalanche-like switching with memory violation.
watch_item: Because bistability and collective memory depend strongly on channel geometry and global hydraulic coupling, device behavior may be highly sensitive to fabrication tolerances and operating conditions.
paper_title: Fluidic hysterons and memory in flow networks
